newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan October industrial production.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan October industrial production.

text.p: The following are reactions of economists and analysts to the trade ministry's announcement on Thursday that Japan's industrial production in October rose a preliminary 3.5 percent from September on a seasonally adjusted basis.
ERIC NICKERSON, VP, CAPITAL MARKETS AND TRADING - ASIA, BANK OF AMERICA, HONG KONG:
"I think these numbers are just going to solidify the mentality that Japanese interest rates and certainly monetary policy aren't going to change any time soon."

Nickerson added that given plans by Japanese life insurers to put more funds into the bond market in the second half, "I think all this points to continued good, strong capital flows and a continued weak tone to the yen."

Asked if he expected the dollar to rise further toward 115 yen after the data, Nickerson said that was a psychologically difficult level to break. "There is sort of a seasonal bias in favour of the dollar now anyway. But I would certainly not be surprised if we test that direction."

"Output forecasts dipping into negative territory in November and in December underscored the prevailing market view that the Bank of Japan is likely keep its easy monetary policy on hold well into the next year."
MINEKO SASAKI-SMITH, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CS FIRST BOSTON, TOKYO:

"Obviously the (bond) market has extended the rally, in my view pretty spectacularly, and bad news would correct the market...(but) I continue to feel monetary policy will be kept on hold for an extended period of time and the economic deceleration will be very apparent after next April.
"Therefore the bond market will remain very, very strong for an extended period of time."
"This number will not have any bad or good influence on the (bond) market. Basically, lots of market participants have a bullish sentiment. Toward the end of the year, the market is going to rally."
